scope: Non-IRIYA Lane C positions 6-32; semantic decisions from complete cases before entry construction.

rows.reason: Changqing's repeated public-interview formula identifies all activity as its functioning and then answers the demand for the body by repeating the function.
The corpus deploys the lion's force as simile, verse-verdict, and name of a samadhi; those are distinguishable concrete-image and named-samadhi senses, not mere containment.
Masters use it as a roster class and evaluative title for tested elders whose conduct or sayings later students are told to examine.

rows.target: trust and mind are not two
rows.reason: The line from the Trust-in-Mind Inscription is repeatedly quoted and then interrogated or capped by Chan authors, who explicitly prevent a facile reading of two items simply becoming one.
Teachers present, demand, sell, or criticize a saying already complete at hand; the Chan bend is whether the respondent can use it without derivative chewing or contrivance.
It is directly asked in interviews and coordinated with darkness-within-brightness as an interpenetrating pair, not a generic lighting description.

Chan masters themselves reuse Zhuangzi's butterfly dream in funeral verse, self/other reflection, and death imagery; the entry must name that inherited allusion and its Chan deployment without importing a doctrinal verdict.

rows.target: the Song of the Purple Fungus
rows.reason: Besides authored verse, the corpus turns the title into a direct test-question and answer; define the Four Hoaryheads' withdrawal song through those Chan deployments.
Biographies and addresses use the idiom for effective action or command without visible disturbance, including Hongzhi's monastery leadership and a capping appraisal.

rows.target: the return path becomes wondrous again
rows.reason: Caodong verse and commentary deploy the phrase for returning from a position without leaving a trace; retained cases both praise and limit the move.
The four recluses are invoked in portraits, place-answers, and public questions; under the figure rule the entry defines what Chan masters do with them, not a free-standing hagiography.

rows.target: polishing a tile to make a mirror
rows.reason: The Huairang-Mazu case and later verses repeatedly wield the impossible manufacture against making awakening by seated contrivance; preserve the case action and its public use.

rows.target: a saying neither dead nor alive
rows.reason: Masters demand it alongside dead and live sayings and answer with a third response; it is a public-interview category, not a paraphrase of either neighboring class.
Manuals, annotations, and verse sequences explicitly name and enumerate this fivefold Caodong scheme; it is distinct from the basic five ranks and must expose that relation.

rows.target: the host responsible for gruel and rice
rows.reason: The corpus uses it both for the actual monastery provider/abbot and critically for one who merely keeps the community fed without carrying the transmission; these are literal and evaluative deployments of the same institutional role.

rows.target: a final address to the assembly
rows.reason: The phrase labels the public deathbed event in which a master tests or charges the community; cases quote Luopu and Linji and also preserve a master's own final address.
Masters award even half an eye as a pointed, often ironic verdict on partial discernment; the corpus also uses the award when both proposed outcomes remain incomplete.
Addresses, biographies, and letters use cutting vines for ending inherited verbal entanglement or hesitation; the blade image becomes a verdict on handling cases.

rows.target: turn the light back and look
rows.reason: Miyun and Yuanwu directly tell students to reverse illumination toward its source when recognition has not occurred; it is a directional instruction, not generic introspection.
Expositions and a direct address say beings never leave this samadhi even in ordinary activity; preserve both the named samadhi and the Chan claim about its unnoticed functioning.

rows.target: sudden awakening followed by gradual cultivation
rows.reason: Multiple works define the sequence explicitly and contrast it with the other sudden/gradual combinations; it names an ordered relation, not two independent practices.

Most cases are ordinary authored verse, but the Lingyun exchange makes 'an accomplished poet' a public verdict on a respondent who can meet the verse; retain that Chan deployment and do not inflate the ordinary occurrences.

All reviewed cases use the ordinary publishing action 'cut printing blocks' in edicts, prefaces, or fundraising notices. Chan books are being printed, but the compound itself receives no observable Chan-specific lexical job.

rows.target: the pivotal action of great function
rows.reason: Masters pair and distinguish great-function's pivot from the function of a great pivot, then deploy it in case verdicts; preserve the coordinated technical relation.

rows.target: the morning of a death anniversary
rows.reason: Records label memorial incense and teaching-hall events held for a late master on the anniversary morning; this is institutional Chan time, not merely a date.

rows.target: hundreds and thousands of hands and eyes
rows.reason: The Guanyin image becomes a verdict that responsive capacities are all exposed at once, while other cases retain the figure's iconographic reference; the entry must keep image and deployment distinguishable.
Masters use the impossible flowering for renewed living function after turning through a dead or exhausted position; it is repeatedly paired with other impossible actions and tested in addresses.
